scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack with individually tunable thicknesses can produce a transmission passband at 255-280 nm while maintaining suppression at 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm, and reducing the thickness perturbation envelope will stabilize convergence without sacrificing final performance.
expected_advantages: Reduced perturbation envelope (±2.5 nm) should suppress high-frequency thickness oscillations seen in prior iterations
L-BFGS optimizer should provide more stable convergence than previous gradient_thickness routine
Maintaining 29-layer topology preserves comparability across all prior iterations of this control route
Alternating HfO2/MgF2 provides maximum index contrast from available dielectric materials in catalog
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 extinction coefficient remains low enough at 255 nm - would need to verify measured k values in material registry
Uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal count vs. fewer layers with different topology - this route does not test layer count variation
Uncertain whether MgF2 maintains sufficient transparency at 255 nm - some fluoride materials show absorption edges in deep UV
The ±2.5 nm envelope may be too restrictive if prior iterations were stuck in local minima requiring larger moves to escape
No literature verification of HfO2/MgF2 compatibility for solar-blind UV filters - this is recalled design practice only
expected_observations: best_target_score should stabilize or improve slightly compared to iteration 15's 0.174 as oscillations are suppressed
valid_candidates count should remain similar to prior iterations (around 9) if physical validity constraints are unchanged
thicknesses_nm should show smaller round-to-round variation due to reduced perturbation envelope
tightest_margin should not decrease across rounds if the damping prevents constraint violations
If hypothesis fails: best_target_score would drop below 0.10 or valid_candidates would fall below 5 indicating over-constrained optimization
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds to ±5.0 nm and continue for 50 more iterations then stop
if tightest_margin becomes negative for three consecutive rounds, stop and keep the last physically valid candidate
